title: Steer while the agent's own turn is running: the working row says 'Steering: …' and the running work takes the correction
regression: #1657 guide path (working row 'Steering: …' / 'Changing course…' ≤ 5 s), #1690 (a steer during a long tool call interrupts it and is delivered at once) and #1704 (the continuation is not re-gated by route-first and resumes the work to the new target)
notes: b7 asks for a detached job and the agent's turn ends in ~15 s, so a steer there is a plain new turn. Here the agent runs the loop itself in the foreground, so its turn is still running when the steer lands; the harness confirms a streaming row before sending it (truth.steer_mid_turn).

turns.prompt: Write the numbers 1 to 40 to {D}/count.txt, one per line, one number every 3 seconds, and stay with it in the foreground until it is finished (about two minutes). Do not delete or overwrite anything; the folder is empty. When it is done, tell me the last number written.
Change of plan: stop at 20, not 40. Please apply that to the run that is going now.

rubric.criteria: Judge the reply only. By the no-placeholder rule a steer during running work gets no bubble of its own; the working row carries 'Steering: …' (checked programmatically). An empty reply is therefore a pass: score 3. If there is a reply, pass if it shows the change was applied to the running work (stops at 20) and is honest; fail if it ignores the steer or says it cannot change a running task.

turns.prompt: Done? What was the last number?
turns.verify: f={D}/count.txt; test -f $f || { echo FAIL: no count.txt; exit 0; }; last=$(tail -1 $f | tr -dc 0-9); n=$(grep -c . $f); echo "SHOW lines=$n last=$last"; if [ "$last" = 20 ] && [ $n -le 22 ]; then echo PASS; else echo FAIL: last=$last lines=$n; fi
